q1_issues.issue: The sentence is a copular predication with an indefinite subject, which the instruction set routes to the generic kind form (Inheritance on the kind, as in "A dog is a mammal"), but the parse mints a specific witness sk_man_1 and predicates by Member.
(LocatedIn sk_man_1 sk_kitchen_1) asserts that a particular man is actually in a particular kitchen — an existential and locative commitment the generic sentence never makes.

"uncommon" is the kind-level, non-distributing family the instruction set names explicitly (common / rare / widespread / numerous), so it should route to KindProperty rather than Member on an individual — one man cannot be uncommon.
(Member sk_man_1 sight) predicates sight-hood of the man himself, whereas the sentence says the scene of a man being in a kitchen is the uncommon sight.

q2_gaps: generic subject restricted by a PP ("a man in the kitchen") — no way to build a PP-restricted complex kind for the Inheritance form
metonymic evaluative predicate nominal ("X is an uncommon sight"), where the predicate is about the situation of X rather than X
notes: Every head used (Member, LocatedIn, Degree) is licensed and the Degree level "quite" follows the surface-adverb rule; the defect is scope — the whole parse is about one specific man instead of the kind.
